newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Slow going.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Slow going.

text.p: Asian debt markets provided a sharp contrast to a hectic day in the European markets, with just a few Asian borrowers launching new issues on Tuesday.
Krung Thai Bank launched a US$100 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue through its Singapore branch.
The straight five year issue pays 42 basis points all-in, in line with expectations. Asahi Finance (Hong Kong), Berliner Bank, BZW Asia and Nomura International (Hong Kong) are the arrangers.
In Tokyo, Taiwan's Mosel Vitelic launched 12.5 billion yen worth of 2.8 percent bonds due in June 2002 at par via lead manager Nikko Securities.
The Asian Development Bank had the biggest deal of the day with its long-awaited US$1.0 billion global bond.
The 6-5/8 percent bonds due 2007 will be priced to yield 18 basis points over comparable Treasuries. SBC Warburg, Goldman Sachs and the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi are the leads.
In ratings news, Standard and Poor's assigned a BB long-term rating to Greater Beijing First Expressways' US$100 million senior notes due in 2004 and its US$175 million senior notes due in 2007.
The bonds are expected to be launched as a 144a issue in the U.S. Morgan Stanley is tipped to be the lead.
The company holds interests through Sino-joint ventures in five expressway projects in the greater Beijing area of China.
